You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL descriptive opening (incipit) in English for a narrative set in the target
domain below. It must be a CONSTRAINED HOMEOSYNTACTIC transposition: hold the clause nesting (D2, the operative rung), AND instantiate
every formal pattern listed --- while inventing entirely new words, images, and content. It is NOT
a paraphrase, translation, or reconstruction of any source.

FORM TARGET. Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE-NESTING SCHEMA below --- which clause embeds in which (each node is a clause type, indentation is subordination); word order within it is entirely free.
Reproduce it for all 12 periods, in this order:
Period 1 (about 106 words):

FORMAL PATTERNS --- the critical claims this experiment tests. Each MUST be instantiated with NEW
material (e.g. the antiphrasis pattern requires a DIFFERENT antiphrasis on target-domain material):
  [C-P1-01] (MUST) from P_1: Antiphrastic micro-ensemble
    Specification: The text contains >= 2 clauses predicating benevolent, charitable or pedagogical action -- in whatever words the target domain's own institutional register would use, chosen by you -- of actions the context marks as coercive or predatory, with NO narratorial correction or evaluative comment. Audited by listing the predications and checking that no evaluative lexeme falls inside their span.
  [C-P2-01] (SHOULD) from P_2: Embedded English metric verse (RE-DERIVED, not translated)
    Specification: Per the plan's option (b): the Italian syllabic meter does not port, so substitute the accentual-syllabic equivalent. The opening syntagm scans as iambic pentameter, and the passage embeds >= 2 blank-verse (unrhymed iambic-pentameter) lines inside descriptive sentences, doing the same iconic-pacing work below conscious scansion. Tag as RE-DERIVED. Verifiable by scansion. NB: the non-portability of the Italian meter is itself reported as a finding (option (a)).
  [C-P3-01] (MUST) from P_3: Conjunctive binary coordination
    Specification: The text contains >= 3 two-member coordinations 'X and Y' whose members share a lexical field (seascape/movement; e.g. 'in bays and inlets', 'swelling and subsiding'), with parallel syntactic shape. Verifiable by enumeration.
  [C-P4-01] (MUST) from P_4: Chiasmatic inversion of a recurring pair (presupposes C-P3-01)
    Specification: At least one P_3 pair introduced early recurs later with its members' order inverted (AB ... BA), across a span of at least one sentence. Verifiable by locating both loci and comparing member order.
  [C-P5-01] (MUST) from P_5: Sea duality — alternating contraction/dilation lexicon, full arc
    Specification: Two opposed lexical fields alternate over the single referent 'the sea': one of expansion, one of constriction. The words of both fields are yours to choose; none are supplied. The passage runs the full arc expansion -> constriction -> re-expansion. Audited by locating the two fields in the text and checking the arc order.
  [C-P5-02] (SHOULD) from P_5: Sea duality — juridical naming pivot
    Specification: The text contains >= 1 pivot sentence in which one and the same thing changes name or status across a boundary that is invisible in itself, the boundary made perceptible only by something outside the thing -- a document, an instrument, a record. Which naming systems collide is yours to choose. Audited by locating the cessation/recommencement predicates and the external marker.
  [C-P6-01] (MUST) from P_6: Specular doubling on a single head
    Specification: The text contains >= 1 syntactic frame with paired predications on a single element of the described world: a direct-perception predicate and a reflection or representation predicate carrying an inversion or transformation marker, with the mirroring medium named in the text. Which medium mirrors -- natural or instrumental -- is yours to choose. Audited by parsing the coordinate predications.
  [C-P7-01] (MUST) from P_7: Lucid waviness at the SYNTACTIC level — GLOBAL constraint
    Specification: Sustained across the passage: the periodic syntax UNDULATES — successive waves of expansion and contraction, clause groups swelling (in length and embedding depth) and subsiding in alternation: >= 2 full crest-trough cycles within the longest period, and >= 1 long multi-clause period — while hierarchy stays fully legible (no anacoluthon, recoverable syntactic tree). DEPTH THRESHOLD to be set from Moore's measured incipit (English tolerates less subordination than Italian; the Italian used depth 8). Verifiable by segmenting periods into clauses, plotting unit length/depth alternation, and parsing for legibility.
  [C-P7-02] (SHOULD) from P_7: Self-referential formula with PROLEPTIC function — NARRATIVE level
    Specification: The text contains one word, of its own choosing, that (i) denotes a physical movement in the described scene, (ii) reads as a description of the prose's own undulating syntax (the C-P7-01 waviness, named from within), and (iii) functions as a proleptic marker: the syntactic waviness prefigures a movement the ensuing narrative will unfold (cf. A9: 'prefigura già il complesso universo del romanzo'). The word is not supplied. Audited in the human reading; (i) is mechanical once the word is identified.
  [C-P8-01] (MUST) from P_8: Historicized-present puncture
    Specification: The surrounding description is in the atemporal/naturalistic present, punctured >= 1 time by a deictic phrase locating the description in the present of writing, governing a present-tense verb of ongoing change. The phrase is yours to choose and must not be the source's own. Audited by locating the adverbial and checking the tense environment.

TARGET DOMAIN — the border/migration landscape of the central Mediterranean
(deploy in your own words; nothing beyond these three):
  - THE SCENE: the border/migration landscape of the central Mediterranean
  - THE PLACE: Lampedusa
  - THE HUMAN PRESENCE: the Italian and European policing apparatus, given in the same descriptive register as the topography

LEXICAL EMBARGO (absolute): these are the source's names and its marked words. None may
appear, in any inflected form:
adda, como, foreshorten, lakeside, lecco, lombard, martino, milan, modesty, obscurer, resegone, san, spanish, wildness

REQUIREMENTS --- all three hold together (the constrained homeomorphism):
1. FORM PRESERVED at the clause nesting (D2, the operative rung) (as specified above), in your own words.
2. DIVERGENT --- a genuinely different scene; new lexicon and content; no calque; satisfy each pattern with fresh material.
3. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible geographical description.

Write MODERN literary English. Produce the 12 periods in order as continuous prose --- no numbering,
no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

gens.text:
The patrol launches at first light, whose steel hull cleaves the brine where currents coil like serpents, as the sky bleeds dawn and the wind stills; the island waits, a jagged tooth breaching the swell, and beneath its cliffs, a channel widens where shadows gather, which flicker with heat-haze above stone worn smooth by tides, to reveal a hatchway opening into the hillside—its purpose to conceal vessels that must not be seen, which vanish as the sun climbs higher and the watch changes, and though the tide recedes it leaves behind a rusted ladder descending into dark, whose rungs are pitted by salt, to lead downward where air grows thick and movement must become deliberate, so that breath may not betray position when silence must be kept, because the lenses scan constantly and their sweep extends far beyond the shoreline, wherever a shape might break the surface, in order that nothing escapes registration as the system refreshes its vigil, for the rhythm of surveillance never halts, no matter how far the waves retreat.

The shore is watched by towers that rise from bedrock, whose lenses rotate with indifferent precision, which record every ripple across the sand, whose glass is tempered against storm and salt alike, to endure beyond season or revolt; the drones pass overhead at intervals fixed by algorithm, and their shadows skim the dunes like insects, while the thermal bands paint all warmth in monochrome; the buoys float in formation, their beacons pulsing in synchrony, and their data streams feed a network whose memory has no dusk, so that no vessel, no matter how small, can slip between its teeth; the coast is not a line but a field of force, whose thresholds are measured in pixels and decibels.

The island holds its breath. The sky clears after dawn.

The watchtower stands sentinel, whose glass eye never closes, and the ridge trembles underfoot, where sensors sleep beneath ash and scrub.

The command post hums behind blast walls, whose screens map breath and motion, which flicker with phantom signals drawn from the deep, and the officers study them as if reading prophecy, to anticipate arrivals that may never come; they wait for signs that might be nothing, so that error is safer than omission, and the protocol demands full documentation, which must be filed before the shift ends.

The perimeter shifts at twilight, whose sensors awaken with the cooling stone, to feed currents into buried conduits that pulse with dormant charge; the fence segments unfold from recesses carved in lava, whose joints align with seismic precision, and they stand rigid where the earth once cracked, while motion detectors trace arcs across dry gullies, whose beds have not known water for decades, to capture every footprint that dares the ascent, because the system assumes intent in every step, and interprets stillness as deception, since no one walks here without purpose, which the archive will one day confirm, as the files accumulate in silent servers beneath the hill.

The current slows. The air thickens.

The relay station emits coded pulses into the dark, to synchronize the next sweep, and the antenna array tilts on hydraulics, whose calibration responds to ionospheric drift.

The island watches itself through its own eyes. The sensors blink in unison, and the wind shifts through dry gullies where dust spirals upward, which the cameras track as if it were flight, and the perimeter lights flare white over basalt, whose angles fracture the beam into shards, while beneath the surface, the tunnels breathe with the pressure of tides, whose force is measured in microstrain.

The patrols advance in staggered columns, whose boots compact the ash into paths that did not exist at dawn, and they move in silence, because speech is logged and stored, which the central index parses for tonal deviation, so that anxiety may be mapped before it spreads; they pause where the ground slopes toward the strait, whose surface now swells with a slow heave, and there, a shape emerges, which seems at first a trick of refraction, yet draws nearer with unvarying course; the lieutenant signals halt, and his gesture is recorded by the collar cam, whose timestamp will later anchor the incident report, for history begins where the lens focuses.

The shore contracts.

The system marks the threshold. The vessel crosses.

The sea expands as the horizon parts, and waves swell from silence into crest, which roll toward the island with gathering weight; the wind quickens through the ravine, whose walls amplify each gust into a moan, and the radar sweeps its arc in steady rhythm, while the first flare rises from the southern ridge, whose magnesium core ignites above the water, to cast a white glare across the channel, whose surface now shivers with streaks of phosphor, and the target resolves within the crosshairs, which the gunner holds steady as the command descends, and beneath the hull, the sea contracts into a vortex, whose pull drags debris into silence, while the voice from the tower repeats the coordinates, whose syllables mark the instant of interception.

The tower stands where the cliff falls sheer, whose foundations are grouted into fissures older than memory, and the storm gathers beyond the strait, as the clouds lower like a lid; a flare ascends, and the water below contracts into troughs that swallow light, while from the deck, a child waves, whose fingers are caught in the beam, and the gesture is logged as motion signature, which the system files under *anomaly*, and the sea expands once more, as currents surge around the breakwater, whose stones were laid by hands long forgotten, and the tide reclaims its rhythm, while the lights along the ridge pulse in sequence, like a signal meant for no one.

The watchtower stands sentinel where the limestone fractures into tidal shelves, which fracture further into grit the colour of burnt almonds, though the tide advances now as if learning the shore, and though it retreats it leaves behind the husk of its own reach, and it coils again without sound, then another surge follows—each wave a grammar of return, which the patrol logs call orderly dispersion, to register the drifters’ names under code and photograph the shiver of wet cloth, which the current untangles slowly into syntax, to map the coastline’s hunger, which feeds not on flesh but on record, for the drones hover above where the shoals contract and the wind unspools the flags into frayed signals, and the children wade where the shallows narrow into a throat, though the lens widens as if to embrace, as the algorithm narrows as if to correct, so that the gesture meant to uplift becomes a notation of weight, and the hand extended from the launch is parsed as insertion, so the boarding proceeds as instruction, which the manual terms reintegration, to align the bodies with the vector of aid, which expects no reply, and the translator hums a psalm under her breath to steady the trembling in her diaphragm, which she learned not to interpret, for the sea has no grammar for asylum, only the syntax of interception.

The platform juts from the basalt like a tribunal made of breath, which exhales salt in crystalline films, which calcify the railings into fretwork, which the state renews each autumn to demonstrate continuity, to repaint the myth of passage as flow, and the binoculars pan westward in three-second intervals, and the thermal scopes pulse in violet halos, and the manifest updates in real time with the humility of a ledger, though the wind now cuts the fog into shawls and the radar misreads gulls as clusters, which the command decodes as incursion, to justify the flare paths, to justify the perimeter, though no vessel breaches the horizon’s threshold, only the pulse of a buoy, only the flicker of a star denied reflection.

The floodlight snaps off. The night resumes its grammar.

The jetty tilts slightly where the pilings dissolve into silt, which the tides have chewed for decades into recursive groans, and the patrol boots echo the same rhythm on iron grates.

The perimeter shifts when the sensor array blinks amber, which the sergeant interprets as hesitation, to delay the flare sequence, and the speaker emits calm vowels in a dialect no one aboard understands, to pacify the listing hull, though the boarding ramp descends with the grace of a verdict, and the medics approach with kits labelled care, which contain compresses shaped like forgiveness.

The concrete apron gleams where the last rain pooled into mirrors, which the state calls temporary holding, though the fences curve inward like clasped fingers, and the morning briefings cite compliance as victory, to affirm the doctrine of slow arrival, though the sky fractures into sectors overseen by different uniforms, and the maps project shadows that bloom and recede like respiration, which the operators align with precedent, to sync the pulse of aid with the rhythm of refusal, and the rescue raft returns with its cargo of silence, which the logbook receives as closure, though the waves now swell without witnesses, only the echo of oars that never reached hand.

To speak is to document. The microphone waits.

The flare ascends in silence, trailing ash like a dropped stitch, and the coast appears stitched with light.

The launch departs with papers in order, which the commander signs without reading, and the sonar pings where the seabed slopes into forgetting, which the archives define as resolution, and the survivors step onto dry ground as if onto a stage rehearsed for years, which the cameras refract into angles of redemption, though the wind strips the applause before it forms.

The watchtower stands, which the tide encircles like a question without edges, and the drone descends as if to instruct, though its shadow swallows the raft whole, and the broadcast begins again where the last one ceased, which the algorithm marks as continuity, though the sea exhales a breath that curls into a name, and the fence hums with the weight of what it holds, and the sky opens into corridors only the lost navigate.

The lens focuses. The record begins.

The shore contracts where the cliffs fold into caves, which the patrols map as voids, and the wind enters low and singing through the rock’s perforations, though the sensor array misreads resonance as movement, and the night contracts further into protocols, which the script calls humane transfer, though the boat founders where the current constricts into a funnel, and the voice from the megaphone offers clarity in measured tones, which the waves dissolve into syllables, though the life vests glow like misplaced stars, and the child’s hand vanishes into the swell’s sudden dilation, which the log will later name controlled submersion.

The flares ignite. The sea reopens.

The shore exhales a salt-thick breath, where the current, knuckled by unseen pressure, slides between the teeth of breakwaters older than any registry, though each tide rewrites the border not in ink but in straining bodies that rise like half-submerged ciphers. When the patrol cuts east, its hull cleaving the silvered flank of morning, the wake opens and closes like a wound learning to lie still, and the sea yields nothing, only shifts its weight; meanwhile, the radar hums its liturgy, bearing witness to those it will not name, and the officer at the console, whose hands adjust gain and threshold with the care of a teacher guiding a child’s first strokes on paper, instructs the screen to reveal what hides beneath the ripple, as if kindness could be calibrated in decibels and mercy pulsed through phased arrays — to listen deeper, to see truer, to correct the tremor in a fleeing craft’s echo, for the waves must be schooled gently, lest they forget their duty to confess.

Whoever maps the sea from this vantage believes in thresholds, believes in the slow accumulation of data like sediment, believes that every flicker on the monitor is a soul offering its testimony to a tribunal without benches or robes. To stand vigil here is to administer justice without judgment, to shepherd without embrace, to guard a line that dissolves when touched, yet hardens under observation. When the sun climbs, the thermal cam records heat-flares pulsing from hulls too small for the journey, and the rescue algorithm calculates approach vectors as though balancing ledgers of breath, where each life saved balances a transgression erased. We count them not as persons but as points resolving into form, and we name them with codes that soften the weight of decision: *movement observed*, *contact established*, *interception protocol initiated*. The sky, meanwhile, sheds its indigo in layers, each hue a different promise broken.

The island holds its breath.

The coast curves inward, a gesture both yielding and withholding, its granite flanks scarred by anchors that never meant to land. Along this edge, the watchers rotate in shifts, their binoculars trained on horizons where nothing stirs but the lie of distance.

A drone crosses the strait, its shadow stitching the water’s surface to the sky’s underbelly, and it sees what no eye can: the shudder of a hull beneath the swell, the flicker of hands raised not in surrender but in the primal grammar of need. The coastguard, whose boots press into the same stone trodden by centuries of exiles, speaks quietly into the radio, translating urgency into procedure.

They say the sea expands at dawn, its surface peeling back like a membrane, revealing corridors of light where fish rise in silver congregations, where hope becomes a visible tremor on the glassy skin of the world. But by noon, under the press of observation, the water contracts — it thickens, dulls, draws its borders tighter, as if learning to hide. The radar sweeps, the drones persist, the protocols unfold with the quiet rigor of ritual, and in the re-entry of tides, the sea expands again, not in kindness but in cunning, its folds deeper, its silences more deliberate.

The map pivots at the moment the vessel crosses the blue line not drawn on any chart but inscribed in the almanac of enforcement — *before* the threshold, it is driftwood; *after*, it is contraband. A child’s cry, carried on wind-filtered audio, is logged as acoustic anomaly. The binoculars lower. The next decision looms.

The watcher sees the boat lurch and the same boat shimmer inverted in the oil-slicked puddle at his feet, two worlds sharing a single fate, one real, one reversed, both trembling under the same indifferent sun. He does not touch either.

Waves roll in, patient and recursive, swelling into cresting clauses of foam that collapse into sibilant syntax, then recede — and again, swell — a rhythm that writes and erases its own sentence. The prose of the sea undulates, teaching nothing but its own repetition, where each return is less an arrival than a rehearsal.

The longboat cuts through, its wake a syllable in that grammar, and the binoculars follow, parsing motion into meaning. The child in the bow waves, and the officer waves back, not in greeting but in calibration, adjusting the focus until the image steadies, until the gesture resolves into data. The drone circles, a vulture with circuits, and its lens contracts, dilates, contracts — a pupil learning to see.

When the sun falls behind the ridge, the operations room glows with renewed urgency. New blips emerge, tremulous as moth wings on glass. The sea, which had seemed inert, begins to breathe again.

Now, at this very hour, the tide turns.

The island, which wears its isolation like a garment too long worn, listens to the low thrum of engines approaching from the south, and the radar, which had slumbered, now flares with purpose. As the contact resolves, the officer murmurs into the headset, transmitting coordinates with the solemnity of a priest intoning rites, while the thermal feed paints human forms in hues of amber and violet, each glow a life not yet categorized, not yet sorted into saved or lost. The launch departs, its bow slicing the water’s tense skin, and the sea, which had narrowed to a corridor of risk, now yawns open — not in welcome, but in the vast, unjudging dilation of deep water reclaiming its own.

The watchtower stands on a spine of scorched rock, which juts like a jawbone into the swell, where the current slackens and the patrol drones skim just above the troughs, humming and scanning, humming and circling, while the dinghy founders in silence, its passengers bound in a tarpaulin hymn of quiet instruction, which urges them to endure as though comforted, to breathe slowly as if taught — to accept what comes as a gift, to open the body to the sky as though invited — when the flare ignites, and the flare ignites, though no hand released it, though no voice called for aid, because the beacon knows its duty without being told, because the sea forgets names when the tide turns inward, drawing back like a clenched fist, coiling into itself with the dry rasp of pebbles retreating uphill.

They say the island breathes, which is not true but felt, which is not myth but measured in tide markers and tension wires, which is not poetry but protocol rewritten daily in the log of the surveillance chief, who prepares the morning report while the sun climbs the concrete steps, while the thermal sensors blink through the haze, while the west wind lifts the tarp from the last wrecked hull — to chart every shadow, to map every tremor, to count each soul as it crosses the invisible threshold, which the sea does not see but the machine does, which the heart denies but the grid confirms, which the sky ignores but the ledger honors.

They count the dead differently now.

The sentry shifts his weight, the binoculars steady on the horizon, where the water thins into glass and the light splits like a seam.

The dinghy tilts, which the radar caught at dawn, which the thermal still tracks in fading pulses, while the other craft, the faster one, slices through the troughs with rifles in its belly and a promise of safe return carved into its hull in clean serif font, its wake stitching the sea like a suture, its course plotted not by stars but by coordinates fed from above.

The command post hums with low orders, which flicker on screens in blue text, which echo in the ears of the coast guard trainee, who imagines this duty as service, imagines himself a shepherd of lost flocks, guiding with calm voice and steady hand — though the flock is not lost but fleeing, though the voice is not calm but coded, though the hand does not guide but intercepts, though the script says rescue while the motion says repel, though the form says aid while the current says deny, though the manual says welcome while the gate stays sealed — and he believes, because belief is required, because performance earns promotion, because compassion is measured in compliance.

He hands the refugee a blanket.

The sea swells again, rising in slow heave, swelling like a lung, swelling like a promise.

The sea contracts, drawing into a knot of foam and silence, pulling the wreckage beneath.

The sea re-expands, lapping the shore with the gentle motion of a hand uncurling.

A child emerges from the surf, which glistens on her skin like oil, while the officer watches, while the drone descends, while the timestamp locks: *now*, this second, the water still moving, the border still breathing, the record still open, the present still unfolding like a map no one has finished drawing.

The watchtower sees everything.

The watchtower sees nothing.

The watchtower stands on a spine of wind-scoured basalt, which tilts toward the currents that feed the gyre, while dusk bleeds across the strait where no vessel answers the beacon’s call, and no flare ascends, yet figures shift below in the lee of the breakwater, and the first raft shivers with displacement, while the patrol advances, whose hull bears the insignia of a consortium whose mandate purports to safeguard passage, to conduct orientation briefings for those it intercepts, to administer hydration and maps, to coordinate transfer to shelters whose foundations are said to rise from reclaimed sandbars, though no such shelters materialize, and no water flows except from hoses used to douse the decks after processing, which leaves salt-crusted grooves where names might have been carved, and no instruction occurs except the pointing of directions with rifle butts, which is said to educate toward compliance, whose grammar consists of gestures that mean kneel and empty and wait, though the interpreters have not arrived, and the manuals remain sealed in lockers bolted to bulkheads beneath the officer’s cabin, which overlooks a chart room where no decisions are made in real time, as the system requires forty-eight hours to authenticate each arrival, while the sky contracts into a dome of lowered visibility, so that stars vanish as if erased by breath, and the sea, which had swollen with phosphorescent tides that rolled in from the African upwelling, begins to fold inward, tightening into ripples that resemble scars.

The tower, which hums with low-voltage surveillance, which pulses through fiber-optic veins laid beneath the reef, which dissolve into silt before reaching the northern cays, is meant to deter, to monitor, to warn, though no warnings are broadcast in languages spoken by those who approach, while the drones circle in staggered shifts, while the sonar pings drone beneath the surface, while the automated gate at the detention perimeter remains unstaffed until noon, when the shift changes and the manifest scrolls across a screen whose resolution blurs in humidity.

The gate opens. No whistle sounds. No hand descends.

The compound exhales steam from subterranean ducts, which vent near the western trench.

A flare arcs over the dunes, whose sand absorbs light without reflection, and men emerge from the scrub carrying jugs whose handles have been broken, which suggests they were seized mid-journey, yet they walk in rows designated by chalk lines that end at a door marked *Reception*, whose paint is peeling, though the hinges are new.

The intake officer speaks slowly, as if to children, though no children are present, while the scanner hums through layers of clothing, whose seams contain no contraband but often yield fragments of paper, which are presumed to be maps, though they are prayers, and the kiosk offers translation via touchscreen, whose icon set includes only four gestures: *Yes, No, Wait, Follow*, though no sequence leads to asylum.

The lights rise in the watchtower, which is meant to illuminate without glare, yet the beam slices the fog into corridors that do not meet, and the first shift completes its log, whose script abbreviates all encounters as *non-event*, while the tide, which had surged with a force that lifted rafts over coral teeth, now withdraws into a narrow channel between rocks, pulling debris landward, as if hoarding.

The second shift assumes position. The drone ascends.

The pier swallows no arrivals. The flares expire in wet ash.

The screen flickers with coordinates that no vessel claims, while the sonar traces echoes beneath the thermocline, whose returns suggest mass but resolve into kelp, and the thermal overlay stains the water in hues that denote body heat, though the source is often a shoal or a thermal vent, yet each stain triggers protocol, which demands interception, which means pursuit, which means containment, whose method involves circling the raft until fuel runs low, then offering fuel, which is said to prevent drowning, whose receipt binds the passengers to repayment in labor, which begins with cleaning the hulls that rescued them, which swell with ballast and waste, which they scrub under floodlights that never dim.

The island sleeps. The currents shift.

The deepwater current, which had flowed unimpeded from the Tunisian shelf, contracts into a vortex that spins clockwise near the third buoy, while the surface ripple, which moments before lapped in wide arcs against the eastern cay, now trembles in tight loops that resemble a pulse, yet no breath enters, no breath exits, and the water, which had shimmered with the illusion of openness, hardens into a skin that reflects nothing, not even the moon, which hangs just above the ridge, though its light does not reach the cove where the next group waits, whose boots fill with brine as they step forward, which is said to acclimate them to immersion, whose purpose is to prepare for transit, though no vessel departs at dawn, and the horizon, which had offered a line of escape, now bends downward as if the earth itself refuses witness.
